summary: The paper measures a known single-learner classification filter (drop training samples whose out-of-fold logistic regression prediction disagrees with the given label, then refit once) on digits and breast cancer with clean labels and two rates of symmetric noise. Under noise, most drops are mislabeled and mean accuracy rises over unfiltered logistic regression in all four noisy settings (not significantly in one), but it stays below clean-label training; on clean labels the cost is small. No new method is claimed.
strengths: The method is easy to follow. Section 3 states the base model, the out-of-fold check, the keep rule (Eq. 1) and what the filter does not need, in a natural order, and the numbered stages of Fig. 1a match that text.
The scope is stated honestly. The paper says it claims no new method, names the weak case and the non-significant case, and lists the controls and methods that were not run.
Checking every drop against the injected flips is a clear idea. Table 1 and Fig. 1b show caught mislabeled samples and lost correct samples together.

The results subsections have headings that state findings, and Table 2 is compact, gives mean and sd with the number of seeds and test set sizes, and bolds the best mean even when it is not the filter.

weaknesses.issue: Table 1 is wider than its column. It runs about 55 pt into the right margin of page 3, nearly to the page edge (overfull box reported for table_drops.tex). This is visible at a glance and breaks the CVPR template.
weaknesses.suggestion: Use a two-level header with 'Digits' and 'Breast cancer' each spanning two columns (with partial rules) and '20%' and '40%' below them, leave the first header cell short or empty, and tighten the column spacing if needed. Check that the overfull box is gone.

weaknesses.issue: The main takeaway is blurred. The abstract, the italic claim in the introduction and the discussion stress that recovery is partial or that clean-label accuracy is not restored, and page 1 never says that the settings differ sharply. Table 1 shows about two thirds or more of the lost accuracy won back in three noisy settings and about a fifth on breast cancer at the higher rate, and Sec. 4.2 itself says 'much of the lost accuracy returns'. A reader of page 1 is likely to conclude that the filter does little. The abstract's 'removes, recovers and costs' also does not say what is recovered until several sentences later.
weaknesses.where: Abstract; Sec. 1, paragraph 3 and contribution 3; Sec. 5, paragraph 1
weaknesses.suggestion: State one scoped headline in the abstract, introduction and discussion: on seed means the filter wins back much of the lost accuracy in three of four noisy settings, but only a small part on breast cancer at the higher rate. Keep the non-significant gain on breast cancer at the lower rate as the one qualifier. Rewrite abstract sentence 3 as, for example, 'We measure which samples one such filter removes, how much accuracy lost to noise it wins back, and what it costs on clean labels.'

weaknesses.issue: The introduction has no gap. It goes from 'noise lowers accuracy' to 'We ask what one linear out-of-fold filter removes, recovers and costs' without saying what is unknown or why a practitioner needs these measurements. Related work then says Brodley and Friedl already evaluated single-algorithm filters, among others, and reported a trade-off between good and bad data discarded. What this paper adds appears only in the last sentence of that related-work paragraph, and contribution 1 repeats the research question.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 1, paragraphs 1-2 and contribution 1; Sec. 2, first paragraph
weaknesses.suggestion: Add two sentences before the research question that say what accuracy alone does not tell a practitioner (how many correct samples are lost, how noisy the kept set stays, how much of the loss returns, what happens when labels are already clean) and that this paper reports these together. Do not claim that earlier work reported none of them unless that is verified. Replace contribution 1 with the filter and the measurement protocol, or merge it into the other two.

weaknesses.issue: Fig. 1c is hard to decode. The axis is the gain of the filter over logistic regression, logistic regression appears as the red zero line, and gray marks labeled 'Clean-label reference' actually show the accuracy that noise costs logistic regression, placed on the gain axis. A reader will likely take them for a clean-label accuracy or gain. The caption needs a convoluted sentence to explain them. The first figure pointer in the paper sends the reader to these marks before the method or the axis has been introduced.
weaknesses.where: Fig. 1c and its caption; Sec. 1, paragraph 1
weaknesses.suggestion: Either plot test accuracy for logistic regression, the filter and the clean-label reference as grouped bars with seed points (the runs behind Table 2), or rename the legend entry to 'Accuracy lost to noise' and add to the caption: 'A bar that reached the gray mark would win back all of the lost accuracy.' Support the introduction's first claim with Table 2, and make the first pointer to Fig. 1 the one to panel (a).

weaknesses.issue: The same findings and caveats recur so often that the paper reads as a list of qualifications. 'Below the clean-label reference' appears in the abstract, contribution 3, the Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 4.2 and Sec. 5. The non-significant gain on breast cancer at the lower rate appears in the abstract, contribution 3 and twice in Sec. 4.2. The phrase 'removes, recovers and costs' recurs in the abstract, the research question and contribution 1. The first discussion paragraph restates results and adds little perspective.
weaknesses.where: Abstract, Sec. 1, Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 4.2, Sec. 5
weaknesses.suggestion: State each caveat once on page 1 and once where its evidence is shown. Cut the repeats from the Fig. 1 caption (now about ten sentences) and the discussion, and use the discussion to say what a user should take from the measurements, within the tested settings. Spend the freed lines on the gap and on per-seed values.

weaknesses.issue: Names drift and slow the reader. 'Ours' is used as a noun in running text ('Ours has a higher mean accuracy', 'the test accuracy of ours minus that of') for a method the paper says is not new. The method is also 'the filter', 'Filter (ours)', 'the refit model', a 'single-learner' and a 'single-algorithm' filter. The baseline is repeatedly spelled out as 'logistic regression with the same settings' or 'trained on all given labels'. The text mixes 'recovers' and 'wins back', 'flipped' and 'mislabeled', and 'established' and 'significant'.
weaknesses.suggestion: Write 'the filter' in prose and keep 'ours' for legends if at all. Define 'unfiltered logistic regression' once in Sec. 3 and use it. Use 'wins back' only, say once that a sample with a flipped label is what the paper calls 'mislabeled', and use 'significant' throughout, which removes the need for the defined term 'established'.

weaknesses.issue: The paragraph on the gap to the clean-label reference is very hard to read: 'borderline', 'just misses', 'just passes it', 'pass it too', 'gap verdicts', 'tentative'. It also calls the gaps tentative while the gains over logistic regression are called established without that word, although Sec. 4 says all these p-values are likely too low.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.2, 'The clean-label reference is not reached' and 'Filtering mostly beats training on all noisy labels'
weaknesses.suggestion: Reduce it to one or two sentences: the filtered model's mean stays below the clean-label reference in all four noisy settings, and tests on overlapping splits are descriptive. Move the p-values to a table row or caption, and apply the overlap caveat to gains and gaps in the same words.

weaknesses.issue: The weak-case paragraph cannot be checked by eye. It speaks of the two seeds where both models are least accurate, but no per-seed accuracy is shown anywhere (Fig. 1c shows only differences), the large sd in Table 2 stays unexplained, and the flipped shares for those seeds sit in the Table 1 caption on another page.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.2, 'Breast cancer at the higher rate is the weak case'; Table 1 caption
weaknesses.suggestion: Add a small five-seed table for breast cancer at the higher rate with flipped share, mislabeled share of the kept set, and test accuracy of both models, all of which come from the saved runs. Move the caption sentence into it. Page 4 has about a dozen lines free before the references, and cutting repeats frees more.

weaknesses.issue: Table 1 row names ('Flipped', 'Left in kept set', 'Correct dropped') are not self-explanatory and differ from the names in the text, so the reader depends on a long caption. The caption ends with a seed-level result that is not in the table. Table 2 repeats the dataset name in each of six headers and shortens 'breast cancer' to 'Breast'.
weaknesses.suggestion: Use row names such as 'Mislabeled, training set', 'Mislabeled, kept set' and 'Correct samples dropped', remove the seed sentence from the caption, and give both tables grouped dataset headers with the full dataset names.

weaknesses.issue: 'Heavier noise costs the filter on both sides' is confusing next to Table 1: on digits drop precision rises clearly at the higher rate and recall changes very little. The reader has to divide precision by the flipped share to see the 'smaller factor', and the 'both sides' are not named as such.
weaknesses.suggestion: Say directly that at the higher rate more correct samples are dropped on both datasets, recall falls slightly on digits and more on breast cancer, and precision rises on digits but falls on breast cancer. Drop the factor argument or add the factors to Table 1.

weaknesses.issue: The MLP paragraph pulls against itself. The heading asserts that a larger model does not make filtering unnecessary, and the last sentence says the gap says nothing about what filtering adds or about larger models in general. The reader cannot tell why the MLP is in the paper.
weaknesses.suggestion: Retitle it with the finding Table 2 supports, for example that on noisy labels this MLP is less accurate than unfiltered logistic regression, so its gap to the filter does not measure filtering. Adjust the question posed in 'Methods' to match, or cut the paragraph to one sentence.

weaknesses.issue: Fig. 1a and 1b have small ambiguities. The pills 'Needs no clean set' and 'Needs no noise rate' sit in the 'Noisy labels' tile, read as properties of the data and crowd the 'Correct label' callout. The five boxes in 'Predict' are never labeled as folds. No boundary shows why the correct sample is dropped. In panel (b), 'Mislabeled' and 'Mislabeled in training set' are easy to confuse.
weaknesses.suggestion: Move the two pills to the caption or below the stage row, label the boxes 'Training folds', draw a dashed schematic out-of-fold boundary in 'Drop', and rename the legend entries 'Dropped, mislabeled' and 'Dropped, correct'. Add one caption sentence saying that the space between the dark bar and the black tick is the mislabeled samples that survive.

weaknesses.issue: The setup interrupts itself. 'Methods' opens with a justification before naming the models. 'Statistics' opens with a sentence about the Scriptorium agent pipeline that says nothing about statistics and, with its named software citation, distracts in an anonymous review copy. The sentence ending 'closer to labels that carry no information than with many classes' is hard to parse, and the number of digit classes is never said.
weaknesses.suggestion: List the three models first, then say which comparison isolates filtering. Remove the pipeline sentence and its reference from the review copy, or place them where the venue's disclosure policy asks. Rewrite the noise sentence, for example: 'With two classes, the higher rate is not far from a coin flip; with ten digit classes, the true label stays far more likely than any single wrong one.'

weaknesses.issue: The clean-label subsection supports 'costs little' with a per-seed range and a one-sample difference but never states the mean differences, and its last sentence ('Neither mean difference is established, which does not show that the models are equivalent') is hard to follow.
weaknesses.suggestion: Open with how far the mean falls on each dataset (recipes for these differences exist), then write 'Neither difference is significant, and five seeds cannot rule out a small cost.'

weaknesses.issue: 'Oracle control' and 'in-sample filter control' are never defined. Section 3 also motivates the design by memorization, which no run measures and which the missing in-sample control would be needed to test.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 3, 'Out-of-fold check'; Sec. 4.2; Sec. 5, 'Limitations and next steps'
weaknesses.suggestion: Define the oracle as dropping exactly the flipped samples and the in-sample filter as checking each label with a model whose training data include that sample. Present the out-of-fold check as a design choice (the checking model has not seen the label it checks) without the memorization argument.

weaknesses.issue: Several references are incomplete: the co-teaching and DivideMix entries print no venue, and the scikit-learn entry prints only a 2012 preprint year.
weaknesses.suggestion: Replace the preprint entries with the verified published records, including venue and year.

questions: Which single message should a reader keep: that the filter wins back much of the loss in most noisy settings, or that a gap to clean-label training remains?
What does this study report about a single-algorithm classification filter that Brodley and Friedl did not report?
Is the sentence on the Scriptorium agent pipeline required by a disclosure policy? If so, where should it go?
Should the MLP stay in a 4-page paper, given that the text says its gap to the filter does not measure what filtering adds?
